name: Mphasis Ltd
title: Mphasis Ltd - 526299 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Mphasis Q4 FY26 revenue $463 Mn, +7.1% YoY cc, FY27 guided high single-digit to low double-digit growth; supply-side signals are absent, with no capacity or utilisation disclosure and OCF/net income guided down to about 80%.

summary.headline: Mphasis Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.1% YoY in constant currency to $463 Mn, with record FY26 net new TCV of $2.1 Bn (up 68%).
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was $463 Mn, up 2.5% QoQ and 7.1% YoY in constant currency, with full-year constant-currency growth of 6.7%. Direct revenue was $456 Mn (98.6% of total), growing 9.2% YoY in constant currency. EBIT margin rose 20 bps QoQ to 15.4% in Q4 and was stable at 15.3% for the year, within the 14.75%-15.75% band. Operating cash flow was $21 Mn, or about $38 Mn excluding roughly $17 Mn of delayed customer remittances collected in early April. Management guided FY27 to high single-digit to low double-digit growth and an approximately 80% OCF-to-net-income conversion.

segments.name: Enterprise Applications (service line)
segments.commentary: Contributed 76.5% of total revenue; Direct revenue grew 5.1% QoQ and 14.8% YoY in constant currency, driven by AI-led modernization programs.

segments.name: ITO (service line)
segments.commentary: Declined 21.6% YoY as the company scaled down non-core ATM business to reallocate toward AI-led opportunities.

segments.name: BFS (vertical)
segments.commentary: Total BFS grew 5.8% QoQ and 15.0% YoY; Direct BFS grew 6.4% QoQ and 17.4% YoY in constant currency, with full-year Direct BFS up 18.6%.

segments.name: Insurance (vertical)
segments.commentary: Direct revenue grew 7.3% QoQ and 46.5% YoY in constant currency, led by AI-driven underwriting, claims and risk use cases.

segments.name: TMT (vertical)
segments.commentary: Saw near-term softness from project completions and delayed decisions; management expects a return to sequential growth in coming quarters.

segments.name: Others (vertical)
segments.commentary: Grew 5.3% QoQ in constant currency, driven by recent Healthcare large deal wins.

segments.name: Geography: US
segments.commentary: Direct revenue grew 3.6% QoQ and 10.7% YoY, driven by ramp-ups of recent large deal wins.

segments.name: Geography: EMEA
segments.commentary: Grew 6.9% QoQ but only 0.8% YoY, impacted by revenue structuring for a large global Logistics client.

segments.name: Geography: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Direct revenue grew 2.6% YoY in constant currency, supported by GCC expansion.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to high single-digit to low double-digit, despite macro uncertainty.
EBIT margin to stay within the 14.75%-15.75% target band while continuing investment in platforms and capabilities.
Operating cash flow to net income conversion targeted at approximately 80% in FY27, described as a floor the company will not go below.
Hedge losses expected to persist through at least H1 FY27, tapering in H2 FY27.
Investor Day to be held in Mumbai in the coming weeks; location and dates to be announced.
capex_capacity: Theory and Practice acquisition (Continuum AI decision intelligence platform) being integrated to extend the AI stack into decision intelligence; CPG and Retail tier-one clients onboarded in production.
Hedge book runs for the next four quarters, so hedge losses continue to weigh on reported margin into H1 FY27.
Working capital investment in large deals (contract acquisition costs and year-one savings commitments) is a deliberate near-term cash flow trade-off.
demand_pricing: Overall pipeline up 38% YoY and 2.6x its initial size since Mphasis.ai launch; 69% of pipeline is AI-led; BFS pipeline up 89% YoY.
FY26 net new TCV of $2.1 Bn (up 68% YoY), the highest ever; Q4 net new TCV was $407 Mn including four large deals, 64% AI-led.
Deals above $20 Mn TCV grew 40% and deals below $20 Mn grew 34% in pipeline.
Top 10 accounts grew 13.7% YoY (3.6% QoQ, LTM basis); next 20 accounts grew 15.2% YoY.
Pricing: management said pass-through of AI productivity gains to clients is partial and structured, with part of savings reinvested into expanded scope; it does not see net deflation.
Client tech budgets have not been cut; tech spend is up low single digits, with large AI infrastructure spend expected outside annual budgets over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: How will clients fund AI transformation that sits outside IT, and when will budgets unlock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no major cuts in pure tech budgets and urgency to act, with spend shifting to AI programs with clear ROI; business-funded programs are framed as revenue plays, not cost plays.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about DSO and OCF conversion, including the $16 Mn that slipped from FY25 into FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: DSO improved by one day; excluding the ~$17 Mn delayed remittance it would be about 86 days, or about 4-5 days better on that basis. OCF/net income is expected at about 80% on a consistent basis; the $16 Mn is roughly 7-8% of PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Can Mphasis differentiate in modernization given vendors are crowding in?
qa_highlights.answer: Differentiation rests on the NeoIP platform, IP assets launched in 2024, and a time-to-market advantage; the Theory and Practice acquisition extends this into business transformation such as underwriting.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the sector seeing dilutive growth from AI deflation, while Mphasis is not?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it passes back only part of productivity gains and asks clients to reinvest the rest in automation and AI layers, using outcome-linked commercial constructs.

qa_highlights.question: How should hedge losses be modelled given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge losses continue through at least H1 FY27 and taper in H2; management says it does not present ex-FX margins and treats the rupee as another variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will BFS growth of about 17% be sustainable into FY27, and what is the outlook for Logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is fairly confident BFS and Insurance can keep driving growth given pipeline build-up, but did not commit to matching FY26 rates. Logistics is expected to recover gradually through FY27, with one or two large wins able to swing the vertical.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin above the band, with rising investment in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said holding margins despite pressure creates room to reinvest in AI, GTM and leadership, and that operating leverage from platform-led models should support the band.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: OCF/net income fell well below the historical 100%+ norm; FY27 target is about 80%, with working capital tied to large-deal contract acquisition costs.
Hedge losses weigh on reported EBIT margin through H1 FY27; a rupee appreciation would reverse the benefit.
TMT near-term softness and Logistics volatility (EMEA YoY growth only 0.8%).
Macro and geopolitical risk, including the Iran war and oil prices affecting transportation and airline clients; management says too early to quantify.
Reporting metric shift: management warned that revenue by delivery location (onsite mix rising) and other legacy metrics may be replaced over 1-2 years.
Dependence on BFS/Insurance growth; non-BFS pipeline growing more slowly than BFS.
Pending Investor Day details and the Theory and Practice integration.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pipeline and AI positioning, with a clear FY27 guide. More cautious and defensive when addressing cash conversion, the rupee/hedge drag and macro risk, with some evasiveness on onsite mix and sector-wide questions.
key_quotes: Over the past year, we achieved our highest -ever annual net new TCV of over $2.1 Bn - representing a 68% increase YoY.
Today, 69% of our pipeline is AI -led, reflecting a structural shift in client demand toward AI-driven transformation.
That's the line we will not cross. And that's what we are targeting.

financial_highlights.value: $21 Mn (about $38 Mn normalised for ~$17 Mn delayed remittances)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided to high single-digit to low double-digit (midpoint ~8%), backed by a record FY26 net new TCV of $2.12 Bn (up 68%) and pipeline up 38% YoY, though no specific capacity additions were disclosed and the brief gives no concrete deal-ramp timing.
